title: Settings' SearXNG and hardware sections are private raw-fetch clients that read once on mount, report every failure as 'sidecar not connected', and never notice a Ready instance that died
repro: Set up SearXNG until the chip says Ready, then stop the container outside the app (or have Docker restart). The Settings chip keeps saying 'Ready - research searches route through it automatically', because status is fetched once on mount (SettingsPanel.tsx:792-802) and polled only while pulling/starting (805-821). Meanwhile research silently rides the keyless fallback. Also: any non-2xx from /search/searxng/status or /system/hardware returns null (707-718; hardware-fit.ts:44-55), and the UI renders 'SearXNG status unavailable (sidecar not connected)' / 'Hardware detection unavailable (sidecar not connected)' (849-853, 1244-1248) even when the sidecar answered with a 500. A failed 'Set up' POST (721-734) collapses to null, runAction re-reads status (823-831) and shows no error.
notes: The component re-implements a sidecar client inline: its own fetch (bypassing sidecarGet, so no X-Vysted-Region or search headers and no extractSidecarDetail reason), a hand-mirrored wire type (SearxngStatus 'mirrors searxng_manager.snapshot()', held in a component, not types/), and its own error policy, where every failure means 'not connected'. It also samples once, unlike StatusChrome's probe, which re-runs on sidecarStatus (StatusChrome.tsx:104-106). The 'Unlimited (Local)' tier is the default research path, and this chip is the one place a user verifies it; a stale Ready hides that research quality has dropped. Smallest fix: add sidecarPost to sidecar-client and route both calls through it; render the SidecarError reason; re-fetch status on panel focus / document visibilitychange or on a slow (for example 30 s) poll while mounted; move SearxngStatus to types/.

refuter.reason: The mechanics are confirmed. Status is fetched once on mount and polled only during pulling/starting. Every non-2xx or throw becomes null and renders 'unavailable (sidecar not connected)'. A failed setup POST shows no error. Fetches bypass sidecarGet. The consequence is smaller than claimed: the sidecar status endpoint re-derives from docker on every call, and research routing does not depend on the chip. The stale 'Ready' therefore lasts only while the Settings panel stays mounted (reopening refetches), and the misleading copy appears only on a sidecar 5xx. Medium becomes low.

title: Anthropic output is hard-capped at 4096 tokens and no layer treats a max_tokens/length finish as truncation
repro: Deep-research synthesis or a long agent answer on Anthropic -> adapter sends max_tokens=4096 (no caller ever sets max_tokens) -> the stream stops mid-sentence with stop_reason 'max_tokens' -> LLMDoneEvent.finish_reason='max_tokens' -> oneshot.complete returns the partial text as the synthesis, agent_runtime only inspects finish_reason=='content_filter', the UI decodes finishReason and never reads it -> a cut-off brief is rendered as complete.
notes: DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS is commented 'Conservative default' but it is the ONLY value ever sent - grep finds no caller passing max_tokens (the runtime allowlists it at agent_runtime.py:102 and nobody fills it). Current Claude models allow far larger outputs; 4096 is small for a multi-section equity brief. The general half is provider-agnostic: finish_reason rides LLMDoneEvent all the way to the browser and is never acted on, so truncation on any provider is silent. In a research product a truncated synthesis presented as final is the data-trust failure the brief UI is built to avoid. Smallest fix: raise the Anthropic default to the model's documented output ceiling (or pass it from the registry), and have oneshot/runtime flag finish_reason in {'max_tokens','length'} as a visible 'answer truncated' note.

refuter.reason: Confirmed: DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS=4096 is the only value the Anthropic adapter ever sends - no sidecar or frontend caller sets an adapter max_tokens (the frontend max_tokens is the Delegate BudgetGuard ceiling, a different field), and oneshot.complete (the deep-research synthesis path) passes no options. finish_reason rides LLMDoneEvent to the browser, but the runtime only acts on 'content_filter', oneshot breaks on done without inspecting it, and the frontend decodes finishReason with no consumer, so a max_tokens/length cut-off is rendered as a complete answer on any provider.

title: ULTRA cross-check prints AGREE over claims the verifier reported UNVERIFIED
repro: python -c "from services.research.verify import _parse_verdict; print(_parse_verdict('UNVERIFIED - no source confirms the 23% operating margin.'))" -> ('agree', ...). The verdict prompt (verify.py:199-207) asks for '<VERDICT> - <reason naming the source domains>', so an UNVERIFIED reason routinely contains 'confirm'/'support'/'consistent'/'match'; _parse_verdict scans the WHOLE first line for markers, agree-markers are checked after disagree-markers but before any verdict-token check. The ULTRA brief then renders '- **AGREE** - <numeric claim> (<domains>)'.
notes: Design-it-twice/obviousness: the prompt already mandates a leading verdict word, so the second design (read the first token) was available and never taken. Consequence: a money-relevant figure (price, margin, ratio, valuation) the verification round explicitly could NOT confirm is published as cross-checked, and verify.py:273 suppresses `detail` on AGREE so the words 'no source confirms' are dropped from the output; `disagreements` (verify.py:396) and brief.note stay silent, so nothing else flags it. test_parse_verdict_is_conservative covers only 'cannot tell from the evidence', so CI is green. Smallest fix: parse the first WORD (head = first_line.split()[0].strip('*:-').lower()), exact-match UNVERIFIED/DISAGREE/AGREE first, fall back to the marker scan only when the head is not a verdict token; add the three proven strings to the test.

refuter.reason: Reproduced exactly: _parse_verdict scans the whole first line for substring markers and never reads the leading verdict word, so 'UNVERIFIED - no source confirms ...', 'UNVERIFIED - evidence does not support the figure' and 'UNVERIFIED - no matching figure ...' all parse as agree. _render_section then prints **AGREE** and suppresses detail on AGREE, and disagreements/brief.note stay silent, so an unconfirmed money figure is published as cross-checked. The existing test only covers 'cannot tell from the evidence'.

title: ULTRA cross-check ignores its budget after the first line; the 90s reserve is decorative
repro: An ULTRA run whose 5 extracted claims each take a slow verdict turn: cross_check() checks budget.breach() once at entry and records once, then runs 1 extract call + N parallel searches + N native calls + N SEQUENTIAL verdict LLM calls with no further breach check and no asyncio.timeout. With _safe_llm's 60s per-call cap that is ~60 + 5x60 = ~360s inside a BudgetGuard(max_wall_seconds=90).

Consequence: the last stage of the most expensive depth opts out of the entire wall-guard apparatus (_PER_ROUND_WALL_SECS, MIN_ROUND_WALL_SECS, per-round asyncio.timeout, the R13 adaptive slice) that exists to kill the 8-minutes-unfinished bug; a 360s ULTRA can run ~270s of panel plus ~400s of verification. Smallest fix: wrap the claim loop in `async with asyncio.timeout(budget.max_wall_seconds)` and re-check budget.breach() before each _verdict_for, degrading the remainder to UNVERIFIED with the reason already used at verify.py:375-378; then correct the docstring.

Added context: the only hard bound is the agent-runtime dispatch guard for 'research' (max(wall, 360, 480)+90 = 570s for ULTRA, agent_runtime.py:579-615,652-667), and an overrun there discards the WHOLE ULTRA brief as a timeout, which makes the unmetered round more costly than stated.

title: ULTRA independence floor double-counts the native channel; one domain can be labelled corroborated
repro: Dual-channel ULTRA claim whose only evidence is ONE domain reached by both lanes: domains = _row_domains(rows) | _row_domains(native_rows) = {d}; independence = len(domains) + 1 (native_text) = 2 >= min_domains 2 -> the verdict runs and, since channels == ['searxng','native'], an AGREE renders as 'AGREE (corroborated across channels)' under an intro promising 'at least 2 independent sources required per claim'.

Smallest fix: `independence = len(domains) + (1 if native_text and not native_rows else 0)` and gate `corroborated` on the two channels resting on DIFFERENT domains.

Severity lowered to medium: the figure still has to be found in the evidence by the verdict pass (it is sourced, from one domain), so this overstates independence rather than publishing an unsourced number; and the +1 is an intentional 'second retrieval path' design (comment at verify.py:371-372) whose flaw is not discounting a native path that cites the same domain.
